### Clustering

In this section, I use the principal components to group the days into clusters. First, I sample the data and cluster it with a variety of methods. I then visually compare the dendrograms to find which method created the most reasonable-looking clusters.

```{r}
# test multiple clustering algorithms

methods <- c(
  "ward.D",
  "ward.D2",
  "single",
  "complete",
  "average",
  "mcquitty",
  "median",
  "centroid"
)

cluster_specs <- map(
  methods,
  ~ hier_clust(
    num_clusters = 4,
    linkage_method = .x
  )
) |>
  set_names(methods)

cluster_specs

fit_cluster <- function(x) {
  x |>
    fit(
      ~ pc1 + pc2 + pc3 + pc4,
      data = weather_data_pca |>
        select(year, month, pc1:pc4) |>
        group_by(year, month) |>
        slice_sample(prop = .3) |> #hclust is slow with large data, so sample
        ungroup() |>
        select(-c(year, month))
    )
}

fitted_clusters <- cluster_specs |>
  map(fit_cluster)

names(fitted_clusters)
```

```{r}
method_tbl <- tibble(method = methods, cluster_fit = fitted_clusters)

get_dendrogram <- function(x) {
  x |>
    pluck("fit") |>
    as.dendrogram()
}

plot_dendrogram <- function(x, method, height_cut = 0) {
  x |>
    as_tbl_graph() |>
    filter(height > height_cut) |>
    ggraph(layout = "dendrogram", height = height) +
    geom_edge_elbow() +
    labs(title = method)
}

plot_dendrogram <- possibly(plot_dendrogram)

method_tbl <- method_tbl |>
  mutate(
    dendrogram = map(cluster_fit, get_dendrogram),
    plot = pmap(list(dendrogram, method), plot_dendrogram)
  )

method_tbl

compare_methods_plot <- method_tbl |>
  pull(plot) |>
  compact() |>
  wrap_plots(ncol = 3)

compare_methods_plot

method_tbl |>
  filter(method == "ward.D2") |>
  pull(plot)
```

```{r}
# Prune a dendrogram to the height at which it splits into `num_clusters`
# branches, returning a tbl_graph with one leaf per cluster (labeled with
# its cluster id and member count).
cut_dendrogram <- function(x, num_clusters) {
  hc <- x |> pluck("fit")
  dend <- x |> get_dendrogram()

  # Cut midway between the heights of the (num_clusters - 1)th and
  # num_clusters-th highest merges, which splits the tree into
  # exactly num_clusters branches
  h_sorted <- sort(hc$height, decreasing = TRUE)
  h_cut <- mean(h_sorted[(num_clusters - 1):num_clusters])

  cut_result <- cut(dend, h = h_cut)

  cluster_assign <- tibble(
    label = hc$labels,
    cluster = factor(cutree(hc, k = num_clusters))
  )

  cluster_sizes <- cluster_assign |>
    count(cluster, name = "cluster_size")

  # Each lower subtree should be cluster-homogeneous at this cut height;
  # identify which cluster it represents
  branch_cluster <- map_chr(cut_result$lower, function(subtree) {
    ids <- unique(cluster_assign$cluster[match(
      labels(subtree),
      cluster_assign$label
    )])
    if (length(ids) > 1) {
      warning(
        "A branch spans multiple clusters; cut height may not cleanly separate clusters."
      )
    }
    as.character(ids[1])
  })

  branch_tbl <- tibble(
    label = str_c("Branch ", seq_along(cut_result$lower)),
    cluster = factor(branch_cluster, levels = levels(cluster_assign$cluster))
  ) |>
    left_join(cluster_sizes, by = "cluster")

  cut_result$upper |>
    as_tbl_graph() |>
    activate(nodes) |>
    left_join(branch_tbl, by = "label")
}

plot_cut_dendrogram <- function(
  x,
  num_clusters,
  method = NULL,
  size_by_members = TRUE
) {
  g <- cut_dendrogram(x, num_clusters)

  p <- g |>
    ggraph(layout = "dendrogram", height = height) +
    geom_edge_elbow() +
    labs(title = method, color = "Cluster") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank())

  if (size_by_members) {
    p <- p +
      geom_node_point(aes(
        color = cluster,
        size = cluster_size,
        filter = leaf
      )) +
      labs(size = "Cluster size")
  } else {
    p <- p +
      geom_node_point(aes(color = cluster, filter = leaf), size = 4)
  }

  p
}

plot_cut_dendrogram <- possibly(plot_cut_dendrogram)

hc_fit <- method_tbl |>

  pull(cluster_fit) |>
```

```{r}
seasons <- c(
  "Winter (dry)",
  "Cool and wet",
  "Spring/Fall",
  "Summer"
)

cluster_pal <- c(
  "lightblue",
  "blue",
  "lightgreen",
  "red"
)

show_col(cluster_pal)

cluster_labels <- tibble(
  .cluster = c(str_c("Cluster", 1:4, sep = "_") |> factor()),
  .cluster_label = factor(
    seasons,
    levels = seasons
  )
)

cluster_assignments <- left_join(cluster_assignments, cluster_labels)

levels(cluster_assignments$.cluster_label)

cluster_centroids <- extract_centroids(hc_fit) |>
  left_join(cluster_labels)

cluster_scatter <- cluster_assignments |>
  ggplot(aes(pc1, pc2)) +
  geom_mark_hull(
    aes(fill = .cluster_label, color = .cluster_label),
    concavity = 3,
    alpha = .05
  ) +
  geom_point(aes(color = .cluster_label), alpha = .1) +
  geom_label(
    data = cluster_centroids,
    aes(label = .cluster_label, fill = .cluster_label)
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cluster_pal) +
  scale_color_manual(values = cluster_pal) +
  labs(
    subtitle = pc_label("pc2") |> str_wrap(70),
    x = pc_label("pc1") |> str_wrap(70),
    y = "PC2",
    color = "Cluster",
    fill = "Cluster"
  )

cluster_scatter

cluster_timeline <- cluster_assignments |>
  filter(yday <= 365) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = yday, y = year, fill = .cluster_label)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cluster_pal) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = 0)) +
  scale_y_reverse(expand = expansion(mult = 0)) +
  guides(fill = "none")

cluster_tree <- hc_fit |>
  plot_cut_dendrogram(num_clusters = 4, method = "ward.D2") +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(3, 7)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = cluster_pal) +
  guides(color = "none")

cluster_plots <- (cluster_scatter +
  cluster_tree) /
  cluster_timeline +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect")

cluster_plots
```

Smooothed timeline

```{r}
test_df <- tibble(
  x = 1:20,
  y = sample(x = c("a", "b"), size = 20, replace = TRUE)
)

find_mode <- function(x) {
  u <- unique(x)
  tab <- tabulate(match(x, u))
  u[which.max(tab)] # which.max always returns a single index
}

test_df |>
  count(y) |>
  filter(n == max(n)) |>
  pull(y)

test_df |>
  summarize(x = find_mode(y))

find_mode(test_df$y)

cluster_assignments |>
  filter(between(row_number(), 80, 110)) |>
  pull(.cluster_label) |>
  find_mode()


smoothed_timeline <- cluster_assignments |>
  select(year, yday, .cluster_label) |>
  mutate(
    smoothed_cluster = slide_chr(
      .x = .cluster_label,
      .f = find_mode,
      .before = 14,
      .after = 14,
      .complete = TRUE
    )
  ) |>
  drop_na(smoothed_cluster) |>
  mutate(smoothed_cluster = factor(smoothed_cluster, levels = seasons))

levels(smoothed_timeline$smoothed_cluster)

smoothed_timeline |>
  ggplot(aes(x = yday, y = year, fill = smoothed_cluster)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cluster_pal) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = 0)) +
  scale_y_reverse(expand = expansion(mult = 0)) +
  labs(x = "Day of year", y = "Year", fill = "Smoothed cluster")
```

## Blog post 2

I train the PCA and clustering on a historical dataset, and then predict the PCA and clusters onto recent data. This makes the PCA and clusters in the context of the historical data.

Approach: fit various clustering algorithms on the historical data and visually inspect the dendrograms to find the best linkage method. Fit that method on the historical data, project the PCA fit (also trained on historical data) onto the recent data, then predict cluster assignments for the recent data.

This produced results that initially looked alarming: cluster composition for several months (summer in particular) shifted dramatically between the historical and recent periods, which seemed disproportionate to the underlying change in the data. Digging into this revealed that the shift is a predictable consequence of using *hard* clustering rather than evidence of an abrupt change in Pittsburgh's weather.

The PC scores themselves move only slightly between the historical and recent periods — means shift by a few hundredths to a few tenths of a standard deviation, nothing dramatic. But once those continuous scores are discretized into hard cluster labels, a small, steady drift can look like a large, sudden change if it happens to cross a decision boundary that a lot of points sit near. That's exactly what happened here: the "summer dry" and "summer wet" clusters are nearly identical on PC1 and are separated mainly by PC2, and enough summer days sit close to that PC2 boundary that a small shift flips a large share of them from one label to the other.

For `ward.D2` specifically, the out-of-sample prediction rule compounds this: `tidyclust` doesn't assign new points by nearest centroid. It assigns each new point to whichever cluster produces the smallest increase in within-cluster sum of squares (Ward's merge criterion) if that point were added — a rule that depends on each training cluster's size and spread, not just distance to its centroid. A naive nearest-centroid classifier only agreed with this rule 70-87% of the time on this data, so the assignment of borderline points can differ noticeably from what a simpler distance-based intuition would suggest.

Neither of these is a bug, and neither is specific to `ward.D2` — it's a generic property of hard clustering. Any method that outputs a discrete label (k-means, other linkage methods, etc.) will show the same behavior: a small, continuous drift that crosses a region of high point density near a decision boundary will register as an abrupt change in cluster membership, even when the underlying continuous measurements changed gradually. Choosing a different linkage method does not fix this, because the discretization itself, not the specific linkage rule, is what manufactures the appearance of a sudden shift.

The practical implication is that hard cluster labels alone aren't a reliable way to characterize *how* Pittsburgh's weather has changed over time — they're good for describing discrete regimes at a point in time, but a sudden-looking change in cluster share should be corroborated against the underlying continuous PC trends (shown above) before being read as a real discontinuity. A natural follow-up, left for a later post, is to track a continuous measure — such as distance to the decision boundary, or soft/fuzzy cluster membership — alongside the hard labels, so that gradual drift and boundary-crossing artifacts can be told apart.

### Predict clusters onto recent data

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| echo: false
# these results seem very extreme. the clusters in recent_cluster_assignments are very different, even though the change in weather over time doesn't appear to be that extreme.

recent_cluster_assignments <- predict(
  hc_fit,
  weather_data_recent_pca
)

recent_cluster_assignments <- bind_cols(
  weather_data_recent_pca,
  recent_cluster_assignments
) |>
  rename(.cluster = .pred_cluster)

recent_cluster_assignments |>
  count(.cluster)

weather_clusters_combined <- bind_rows(
  cluster_assignments |> select(-.cluster_label),
  recent_cluster_assignments
) |>
  left_join(cluster_labels, by = ".cluster")

glimpse(weather_clusters_combined)

#issue with cluster prediction on new data is caused by PCA prediction?
weather_clusters_combined |>
  select(date, starts_with("pc")) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("pc")) |>
  ggplot(aes(date, value)) +
  geom_smooth() +
  facet_wrap(vars(name), scales = "free_y")

weather_clusters_combined |>
  count(decade, .cluster, .cluster_label)

weather_clusters_combined |>
  count(.cluster, .cluster_label)

weather_clusters_combined |>
  ggplot(aes(x = yday, y = year, fill = .cluster_label)) +
  geom_tile() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1990) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(0)) +
  scale_y_reverse(expand = expansion(0)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cluster_pal) +
  labs(
    title = "Cluster analysis of Pittsburgh seasons",
    subtitle = "Clustering trained on pre-1990 data, predicted onto post-1990 data",
    x = "Day of year",
    y = "Year",
    fill = "Cluster"
  )

cluster_summary <- weather_clusters_combined |>
  mutate(decade = year(date) %/% 10) |>
  filter(year != max(year)) |>
  summarize(
    avg_start = mean(min(yday)),
    avg_end = mean(max(yday)),
    days = n(),
    .by = c(.cluster, year)
  ) |>
  left_join(cluster_labels)

cluster_summary |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = days, fill = .cluster_label)) +
  geom_area() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cluster_pal) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = 0)) +
  labs(
    title = "Days of year per cluster",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Days",
    fill = "Cluster"
  )

cluster_summary |>
  pivot_longer(cols = -c(.cluster, .cluster_label, year)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = value, color = .cluster_label)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .2) +
  geom_smooth() +
  facet_wrap(vars(name), scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = cluster_pal) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Day of year")
```
